body.text: Some regiments lose a match. Others lose a match, book a second one, and then lose that too, on the same weekend, to two entirely different opponents. The USAR 75th Ranger Regiment's Scrim Team have this week achieved the rare double, falling first to the RAF 1 Commando Scrim Team and then to the Close Protection Unit, in a pair of 5v5 engagements that observers have described as "thorough."

Credit where it is due. The Rangers' 458 represents a colossal improvement on their previous outing against the Commandos, in which they managed 101 and a thousand-yard stare. At this rate of growth they are on track to win a scrim sometime around the middle of next year, assuming the Commandos agree to stand very still.

The Commandos, for their part, appeared to treat the fixture as a light cardio session. Flanks were run. Angles were held. At one point a Commando player reportedly pushed an entire site alone, apparently under the impression the round had already ended.
"They made us work for it," said one Commando, in a tone that suggested he had not worked for it.
Match Two: The Close Protection Unit Arrives
If the Commando match was a lesson, the CPU match was a fixture list error. 750-165. The Rangers were, at several points, outscored by their own respawn timers.

The CPU declined to give a lengthy statement, saying only that they had "prepared extensively" and then declining to specify for what. Analysts reviewing the demo have so far been unable to identify a single Ranger strategy.
Following the matches, the 75th Ranger Regiment accused at least 1 player of cheating.

This has been checked, it has been checked more than once. It has been checkled by people who were keen to find something and did not. What the review did establish is that the Rangers may suffer from a severe case of "skill issue".
The 75th Ranger Regiment have not commented further. The Commandos have moved on. The CPU have, as far as anyone can tell, gone back to whatever it is the CPU do whenever they are not doing this.
Fish News will continue to monitor the situation, though at this stage we are less reporting on a rivalry and more maintaining a ledger.
